biggest_catch: Day begins ~6:30 AM (5:30 for Tuesday elections) and ends only after poll closing duties are completed after 8:00 PM; you must first attend commissioner's school and pass a written exam to be certified.
catches: $200/day is the regular election commissioner rate; commissioner-in-charge ($250/day) requires separate certification, two prior elections served, and selection for a one-year term.

Must be a registered qualified voter in East Baton Rouge Parish; must not have been convicted of an election offense; must be able to perform all essential duties in the Secretary of State's Informational Pamphlet.
Must attend commissioner's school and pass the written exam to be certified; duration of the school is not stated, so it is not counted in the time estimate.
Work begins approximately 6:30 AM (5:30 AM for Tuesday elections) and ends after poll closing duties following the 8:00 PM close; exact end time varies by precinct.
In the 2026 session, Louisiana HB 205 would authorize parishes to add up to $100/day supplemental compensation; the parish brochure reflects no supplement, so $200 is used.

steps: Confirm you are a registered qualified voter in East Baton Rouge Parish with no election-offense convictions and able to perform all essential duties in the Secretary of State's Informational Pamphlet.
Contact the East Baton Rouge Parish Clerk of Court Elections Department at (225) 295-4765 or elections@ebrclerkofcourt.org for information on becoming an election commissioner.
Attend a commissioner's school and pass the written exam to become certified as an election commissioner.
Await drawing by the Parish Board of Election Supervisors for an election assignment.
Report to the assigned precinct at approximately 6:30 AM (5:30 AM for Tuesday elections) on Election Day.
Serve through the 8:00 PM close and complete all poll closing duties; receive $200 per day.
timing: Election Day: approximately 6:30 AM (5:30 AM for Tuesday elections) until poll closing duties are completed after 8:00 PM.
weasel_words: Commissioner's school is required for certification but its duration is not stated, so no time is counted for it.
Exact end time depends on poll closing duties at the precinct; estimated ~9:00-10:00 PM.
Louisiana HB 205 (2026 session) would authorize parishes to add up to $100/day supplemental compensation; the parish brochure reflects no supplement, so $200 is used.
Commissioners-in-charge are selected separately for a one-year term; this route represents the regular $200/day commissioner.
